LanguageData.SettlementServices.Settings.WealthPriceS: Multiplies the wealth-based portion of every service's price (each service adds a small percentage of your total colony wealth on top of its minimum cost; this scales that percentage up or down). 100% leaves service pricing at its default balance.
LanguageData.SettlementServices.Settings.GoodwillDisc: Scales how much a settlement's price discounts to you at +20/+40/+60/+80/+100 goodwill. 100% is the default balance; 0% removes goodwill's effect on price entirely.
LanguageData.SettlementServices.Settings.NegotiatorSo: Grants a discount on service quotes based on the caravan's negotiator's effective Social skill: 2% at 5, 3% at 10, 4% at 15, and 5% at 20. Switching this off removes the discount from future quotes.
LanguageData.SettlementServices.Settings.InvestmentCo: Scales the silver cost of investing in a settlement (default: 1% of total player wealth x the difficulty multiplier).
LanguageData.SettlementServices.Settings.InvestmentDi: Scales the discount a fresh investment grants (default: 15% off, before decay).
LanguageData.SettlementServices.Settings.InvestmentDe: Scales how long an investment takes to fully decay (default: about 30 in-game days).
LanguageData.SettlementServices.Settings.StockQuantit: Scales the capacity and per-refresh replenishment of the stock this mod's settlements hold, including mechanoid hiring stock. Refresh intervals, which goods are stocked, service input costs, and prices are unchanged, and vanilla trader inventories are not affected. 1× is the default balance. Stock that already exists is not topped up retroactively; it fills through future refreshes, and lowering the multiplier caps existing stock at the new limit.
LanguageData.SettlementServices.Settings.SpecialtiesN: These settings apply to all saves and only affect settlements that have not yet received their specialties, or whose owner changes. Settlements that already have specialties keep them. A settlement can never receive more specialties than it is eligible for, and with zero specialties, services that depend on a specialty are unavailable there.
LanguageData.SettlementServices.Settings.SpecialtyCou: Added to the number of specialties a settlement starts with, after the chances below have decided that number. Negative values remove specialties, down to zero. 0 is the default balance.
LanguageData.SettlementServices.Settings.SpecialtyCha: Chance of starting with one specialty: {0}%
Chance of starting with two specialties: {0}%
Chance of starting with three specialties: {0}% (the remainder)
The chances of starting with one, two, or three specialties always add up to 100%. The chance of three is whatever remains after the first two. The default is 65% / 30% / 5%.
LanguageData.SettlementServices.Settings.SpecialtyPre: With these settings, settlements that start with one, two, or three specialties end up with {0}, {1}, or {2} respectively, before being limited to the specialties they are eligible for.
LanguageData.SettlementServices.Settings.DifficultyMu: Multiplies the wealth-based price surcharge when this difficulty is active. 100% applies no extra scaling beyond the wealth-based surcharge itself.
LanguageData.SettlementServices.Settings.MoodBuffsRes: These values are only copied into this mod's memory thoughts when Settlement Services initializes. Restart Rimworld after changing them for the new values to take effect.
LanguageData.SettlementServices.Settings.MoodBuff.Too: Sets this mod's own memory's mood bonus. A value of zero disables this specific mood bonus. Vanilla thoughts (including Lodging's own) are never affected. Requires a game restart to take effect.
LanguageData.SettlementServices.Settings.ServiceEvent: How often paid services can trigger a bonus or complication beyond their normal outcome, relative to each service's own default rate.
LanguageData.SettlementServices.Settings.SoundtrackEn: Fade in a short ambient loop while browsing a settlement's services menu, and fade normal music back in when you close it.
LanguageData.SettlementServices.Settings.VerboseLoggi: Write Settlement Services' internal diagnostic messages to the log, without needing a debug build. Intended for troubleshooting; leave off for normal play.
